display_contract.front: Arabic script only; no translation, English question, transliteration, definition, or hint.
display_contract.back: All translations, definitions, examples, grammar/register data, metadata, and eight layered fields.
display_contract.retrieval_direction: Arabic -> meaning/use first; alternate representations are scheduled separately.

cards.title: مَرْحَبًا
cards.definition_ar: تَحِيَّةٌ عامَّةٌ تُقالُ عِندَ لِقاءِ شَخصٍ.
cards.definition_en: A general greeting used when meeting someone.

layers.concept_expansion: A common Standard Arabic greeting not tied to a specific time of day.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: By itself مرحبا commonly functions as ‘hello’; do not restrict it to the English sense of ‘welcome.’
layers.connections_and_memory: Connect it with أَهْلًا and السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ as other greeting choices.
layers.transfer_prompt: Enter an evening study group and greet everyone with a time-neutral MSA greeting.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize مَرْحَبًا in audio, give its meaning, and use it naturally in a new greeting.

cards.title: كَيْفَ
cards.definition_ar: اسْمُ اسْتِفْهامٍ يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلسُّؤالِ عَنِ الحالِ أَوِ الطَّريقَةِ.
cards.definition_en: An interrogative word used to ask about condition or manner: ‘how.’

layers.concept_expansion: It is a high-frequency interrogative. In كَيْفَ حالُكَ؟ it asks about a person’s state or condition.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: كَيْفَ حالُكِ؟ — How are you? (to a woman)
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not force a word-for-word English translation onto every Arabic expression; كيف حالك is idiomatically ‘How are you?’
layers.transfer_prompt: Use كَيْفَ to ask how someone is, then form one other simple ‘how’ question.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize كَيْفَ in speech and use it productively rather than only translating it.

cards.title: أَنْتَ / أَنْتِ
cards.definition_ar: أَنْتَ ضَميرُ المُخاطَبِ المُفْرَدِ المُذَكَّرِ، وأَنْتِ ضَميرُ المُخاطَبَةِ المُفْرَدَةِ المُؤَنَّثَةِ.
cards.definition_en: أنتَ addresses one male; أنتِ addresses one female.
cards.example_en: And you? (to a man / to a woman)

layers.direct_answer: أَنْتَ = singular masculine ‘you’; أَنْتِ = singular feminine ‘you.’
layers.concept_expansion: MSA marks the gender of a singular addressee in the second-person pronoun; the final vowel distinguishes the forms.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: وَأَنْتَ؟ to a man; وَأَنْتِ؟ to a woman.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: English/Urdu/French translation can hide the Arabic gender distinction, so retrieve the Arabic form directly.
layers.connections_and_memory: The same contrast reappears in attached suffixes such as ـكَ / ـكِ.
layers.transfer_prompt: Say ‘And you?’ first to one man and then to one woman.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce and recognize both forms without relying on translation.

cards.title: كَيْفَ حالُكَ؟ / كَيْفَ حالُكِ؟

translations.ur: آپ کیسے ہیں؟ / آپ کیسی ہیں؟

cards.definition_ar: سُؤالٌ عَنِ الحالِ؛ تُسْتَعْمَلُ ـكَ لِلمُذَكَّرِ وَـكِ لِلمُؤَنَّثِ.
cards.definition_en: A question about someone's condition; use -ka for a male addressee and -ki for a female addressee.
cards.example_en: Hello, how are you? (to a woman)

layers.direct_answer: To a man: كَيْفَ حالُكَ؟ To a woman: كَيْفَ حالُكِ؟
layers.concept_expansion: حال means state/condition. The attached suffix means ‘your’: ـكَ masculine singular, ـكِ feminine singular.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: كَيْفَ حالُكَ يا مُحَمَّد؟ / كَيْفَ حالُكِ يا مَرْيَم؟
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Without full vowel marks, كيف حالك can look identical in writing; pronunciation depends on the addressee.
layers.connections_and_memory: أَنْتَ/أَنْتِ and ـكَ/ـكِ encode the same masculine/feminine addressee contrast.
layers.transfer_prompt: Ask an imagined man and woman how they are, changing only what gender requires.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce both forms with the correct ending and explain why they differ.

cards.title: بِخَيْر
cards.definition_ar: تَعْبيرٌ يَعْني أَنَّ الشَّخْصَ في حالٍ جَيِّدَةٍ.
cards.definition_en: An expression meaning that someone is doing well or is in a good condition.

layers.concept_expansion: It expresses being in a good state and can stand as a concise response without an explicit pronoun.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not require an explicit أنا every time; Arabic can answer simply بِخَيْر.
layers.connections_and_memory: The root خ-ي-ر carries ideas of goodness and well-being.
layers.transfer_prompt: Someone asks how you are; answer naturally without copying English full-sentence structure.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize بِخَيْر instantly in audio and use it as a natural response.

cards.title: الْحَمْدُ لله

translations.en: praise be to God; thank God
translations.fr: Dieu soit loué ; grâce à Dieu

cards.definition_ar: عِبارَةُ حَمْدٍ وَشُكْرٍ لله، وتُسْتَعْمَلُ كَثيرًا لِلتَّعْبيرِ عَنِ الامْتِنانِ.
cards.definition_en: A formula of praise and thanks to God, commonly used to express gratitude.

layers.direct_answer: الْحَمْدُ لله = praise be to God / thank God.
layers.concept_expansion: In this lesson it follows بِخَيْر as a common expression of gratitude for well-being; it is used in many other everyday and religious contexts.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: بِخَيْر، الْحَمْدُ لله. — Fine, thank God.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: It is not merely a generic equivalent of English ‘thanks’; the praise/thanks is directed to God.
layers.connections_and_memory: Root ح-م-د links حَمْد and names such as مُحَمَّد and أَحْمَد.
layers.transfer_prompt: Use الْحَمْدُ لله after answering how you are, then think of another natural context for it.
layers.mastery_evidence: Understand it in audio, explain its meaning, and use it appropriately rather than as a generic filler.

cards.title: وَأَنْتَ؟ / وَأَنْتِ؟
cards.definition_ar: سُؤالٌ قَصيرٌ يُعيدُ السُّؤالَ إلى المُخاطَبِ؛ أَنْتَ لِلْمُذَكَّرِ وَأَنْتِ لِلْمُؤَنَّثِ.
cards.definition_en: A short phrase that returns the question to the other person; أنتَ is masculine and أنتِ feminine.
cards.example_en: I'm fine, and you? (to a woman)

layers.direct_answer: To a man: وَأَنْتَ؟ To a woman: وَأَنْتِ؟
layers.concept_expansion: وَ means ‘and,’ followed by the gendered second-person singular pronoun.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not pronounce both forms the same; the final vowel marks the addressee’s gender in MSA.
layers.connections_and_memory: This reinforces the same أَنْتَ/أَنْتِ distinction used throughout second-person grammar.
layers.transfer_prompt: Answer ‘I'm fine, thank God, and you?’ first to a man and then to a woman.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce both versions smoothly as part of a greeting exchange.

cards.title: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ ↔ وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام

translations.en: Peace be upon you / And upon you be peace
translations.fr: Que la paix soit sur vous / Et sur vous la paix

cards.definition_ar: تَحِيَّةٌ شائِعَةٌ، وَجَوابُها المَأْلوفُ وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام.
cards.definition_en: A very common greeting meaning ‘Peace be upon you,’ with the conventional reply ‘And upon you be peace.’
cards.example_en: Peace be upon you. — And upon you be peace.

layers.direct_answer: Greeting: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. Conventional reply: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام.
layers.concept_expansion: It is an all-purpose greeting used widely in Arabic-speaking and Muslim contexts.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: The conventional response begins وَعَلَيْكُمُ and reverses the order rather than merely repeating the greeting.
layers.connections_and_memory: Root س-ل-م connects ideas of peace and safety and words such as سَلام.
layers.transfer_prompt: Hear the greeting unexpectedly and give the conventional response immediately.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize the greeting at natural speed and produce the response automatically.
